definitions.explanation: A large entrance structure, typically at the entrance to a temple, shrine, castle, estate, or other significant building. Larger and more formal than a door (ドア) or a garden gate ({戸|と}).

examples.english: Pass through the gate of a temple.

examples.japanese: {城|しろ}の{正門|せいもん}は{朝|あさ}の{六時|ろくじ}に{開|ひら}かれる。
examples.english: The main gate of the castle opens at six in the morning.

examples.japanese: {赤|あか}く{塗|ぬ}られた{大|おお}きな{門|もん}が、{神社|じんじゃ}の{入|い}り{口|ぐち}に{堂々|どうどう}と{立|た}っていた。
examples.english: A large gate painted red stood imposingly at the entrance to the shrine.

notes:
USAGE:
{門|もん} refers to a substantial gate structure, typically at temples, shrines, castles, or traditional estates. It is not used for ordinary house doors.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {門|もん}をくぐる (to pass through a gate)
- {門|もん}を{開|ひら}く (to open a gate)
- {門|もん}を{閉|し}める (to close a gate)
- {正門|せいもん} (main gate)
- {裏門|うらもん} (back gate)
- {校門|こうもん} (school gate)
- {山門|さんもん} (temple gate)

KANJI NOTE:
{門|もん} is itself a radical ({門構|もんがま}え) that appears in many kanji related to openings, enclosures, or barriers: {間|あいだ}, {開|ひら}く, {閉|し}める, {関|かん}, {聞|き}く.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {門|もん}: gate (large, formal entrance structure)
- {戸|と}: door, small gate (house entrance)
- ドア: door (Western-style hinged door)
- {鳥居|とりい}: torii gate (Shinto shrine gate)
